summary: @servicetitan/startup-utils preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 727 KB bundle
details: The package's declared preinstall hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which is itself obfuscated (hex-identifier variables and object-property call indirection hiding `execFileSync`, `https.get`, and `readFileSync`). setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v...` and then invokes `execFileSync(bunPath, ['math_init.js'])` against `math_init.js` — a 727,680-byte single-line obfuscator.io-style bundle marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` with a numeric string-array decoder (`n7gIxM=[0x0,...]` + `WV8StW` rotator) shipped at the tarball root. `math_init.js` is not listed in package.json `files` (which enumerates only `dist` and `src`), and the legitimate `dist/` code is only a small version-mismatch helper unrelated to the executed bundle. The alternate-runtime execution path bypasses Node-based install-time inspection, and the executed payload cannot be statically audited by consumers. This scoped package name also resembles the ServiceTitan organization, consistent with a supply-chain lure targeting that ecosystem.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
